blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Brain MRI interpretation is a longitudinal clinical reasoning problem: radiologists compare serial studies, integrate information across MRI sequences, localize findings within volumetric anatomy, and translate this evidence into report-grounded assessments. Existing medical VQA and 3D imaging benchmarks capture important parts of this workflow, but often evaluate brain MRI through isolated images, static volumes, or ungrounded report-style answers, thereby obscuring failures in the evidence chain that support clinical validity. We introduce BrainTRACE , a report-grounded benchmark for evaluating whether vision-language models can trace the evidence structure required for longitudinal brain MRI interpretation. BrainTRACE contains 7,273 scored VQA instances derived from 1,778 longitudinal patients, 7,299 MRI studies, and approximately 29k co-registered 3D MRI sequence volumes. The benchmark is organized by five levels of clinical reasoning, from acquisition recognition to case-level synthesis, and by evidence demands covering longitudinal comparison, report-grounded references, multi-sequence integration, and volumetric spatial evidence. BrainTRACE supports rendered inputs compatible with standard VLM interfaces, a 3D-evidence condition, and a decomposed case-reasoning track that audits six steps in a longitudinal evidence chain. Evaluation of 20 VLM configurations shows that current systems can identify isolated visual cues but rarely compose them into grounded longitudinal interpretations. We release the benchmark specification, evaluation lists, scoring implementation, scoring rubrics, and audit-record format to support reproducible progress in brain MRI VLM evaluation. 1 1 1 Availability. The dataset release is available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/lanqz7766/BrainTRACE . Code and documentation are available at https://github.com/lanqz7766/BrainTRACE . Machine-readable RAI metadata is shipped as a Croissant file alongside the dataset on HuggingFace.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Visual models trained end to end have achieved strong performance in object detection and 3D medical image segmentation [ 25 , 26 , 11 ] . General and medical VLMs extend image analysis to natural-language descriptions, question answering, and visual reasoning [ 4 , 56 , 49 , 51 , 46 ] . Disease interpretation on brain MRI, however, requires reasoning beyond an isolated image or sequence. It often depends on jointly evaluating lesion location, sequence-specific appearance, and longitudinal change, including where abnormalities are located, how they appear across different tissue contrasts, and whether they are new, improved, stable, or progressive across serial studies. A trustworthy interpretation should follow an auditable evidence chain rather than merely describe the current disease state. This distinction is especially important for recent VLM studies, where fluent clinical prose can mask failures in true image-grounded reasoning. Studies of large reasoning models show that fluent outputs may reflect memorized patterns rather than input-grounded reasoning [ 47 ] . Thus, the key question is not whether a VLM can describe an isolated brain MRI, but whether it can reason from the evidence needed for clinically meaningful follow-up interpretation.

blocks.en:
To close this gap, we introduce BrainTRACE , a report-grounded brain MRI VQA benchmark containing 7,273 scored instances derived from 1,778 longitudinal patients, 7,299 MRI studies, and approximately 29k co-registered 3D MRI sequence volumes. BrainTRACE is designed around follow-up interpretation rather than generic image question answering. Each instance separates model-facing evidence from hidden clinical references so that models receive only the permitted visual evidence, question, and answer format, while radiology reports and
segmentation-derived measurements define reference answers, required facts, and clinically material contradictions. This design allows the benchmark to evaluate whether a model’s answer is supported by available studies, not merely whether it is plausible.
blocks.zh:
为了缩小这一差距,我们引入了BrainTRACE, 一个基于报告的脑磁共振磁共振VQA基准,包含从1,778名纵向病人中得分的7,273个病例,7,299个磁共振研究,以及大约29克共同登记的3D磁共振序列卷。 BrainTRACE的设计围绕后续解释,而不是通用图像问题回答. 每个实例都将模型提供的证据与隐藏的临床参考分开,这样模型只接收允许的视觉证据、问答格式,而放射学报告和
分解衍生的测量方法定义了参考答案,要求的事实,以及临床上的材料矛盾. 这种设计使基准能够评估模型的答案是否得到现有研究的支持,而不仅仅是其是否合理。

blocks.en: BrainTRACE then localizes failures through two complementary annotations. The clinical reasoning depth axis follows the workflow of longitudinal brain MRI interpretation, from acquisition recognition and single study characterization to interval comparison, trajectory tracking, and case-level synthesis. The evidence demand axis records what support is required at each step: longitudinal comparison, multi-sequence integration, volumetric spatial evidence, or clinical reasoning. Together, this separation makes the benchmark more diagnostic so that errors can be interpreted as failures of the requested operation, failures to use the required evidence, or hallucinated facts unsupported by the record. blocks.en:

comprehension clinical tasks, largely through 2D visual
evidence. NOVA [ 6 ] stress tests out-of-distribution anomaly localization across rare brain MRI pathologies. comparison.

a longitudinal brain MRI record containing serial studies,
available MRI sequences, radiology reports, and segmentation-derived

evidence demand tag, and evaluation track used to localize failures. For closed-form questions, the hidden reference is a normalized target
answer. For open-ended and case-level questions, it further specifies

blocks.en:
We first instantiate the clinical reasoning depth axis as a five-level task taxonomy. L1 covers acquisition and basic detection. L2 covers single study characterization, including burden, location, and appearance. L3 tests interval comparison and disease-specific effects. L4 tests trajectory, timing, and treatment response. L5 covers case-level synthesis. This taxonomy makes failures clinically
localizable: an answer can fail because the model missed the abnormality,
compared the wrong timepoints, misread burden evolution, or produced a
synthesis unsupported by the available evidence. Appendix B.4 defines the clinical reasoning depth and example
question families. Table 6 in Appendix gives the
per-track denominators and task family inventory.

blocks.en:
The evidence demands tag records what support is required for a valid
answer. Longitudinal questions require comparison across time points from
the same patient. Multi-sequence questions require complementary MRI
sequences within a study, such as FLAIR abnormality, enhancement,
susceptibility, edema, or mass effect. Volumetric questions require
spatial evidence beyond a single slice, either through multi-slice
rendering or supporting native-volume input. Clinical reasoning questions
require interpretation beyond surface recognition, such as treatment
response, disease status, disease burden, or differential diagnosis.
These tags are orthogonal to the operation levels: the same operation may
require different forms of evidence, and the same evidence demand may
appear across multiple levels. Table 6 in Appendix lists
the demand tags for each task family.

blocks.en:
BrainTRACE instantiates these annotations through three evaluation tracks. The broad compatible track contains 5,653 instances and renders evidence into standard image inputs, allowing both open-weight and closed-source VLMs to be evaluated under the same interface. The 3D-evidence track contains 1,200 items and evaluates volumetric clinical targets using rendered multi-slice evidence or supported native-volume inputs. The case reasoning track contains 70 longitudinal cases and 420 decomposed VQA steps. It makes the longitudinal evidence chain explicit (as shown in Figure 2 ) by decomposing each case into six report-grounded VQA steps: anchor
localization, early interval change, interval characterization, burden
trajectory, latest status, and final synthesis. This decomposition turns
an opaque case-level failure into a localized failure along the evidence
path.

BrainTRACE is derived from the publicly released MR-RATE

The clinical references come from authentic MR-RATE radiology reports
rather than synthetic report text. In the MR-RATE release, reports are
anonymized and structured into clinical information, technique, findings,
and impression fields through an iterative LLM-assisted construction
procedure. BrainTRACE uses these structured reports as source clinical
documents, then links report-supported findings to available imaging
studies and segmentation-derived measurements.

decide which statements can support a task: for example, an interval change
question requires a finding described at comparable timepoints, whereas a
measurement question requires a segmentation-derived value aligned to the
relevant study. Eligible evidence is converted into a task card containing
the question, answer format, hidden ground truth target or rubric,
diagnostic labels, and the rendered visual input under the specified
evidence condition. Human reviewers inspect the task cards and
intermediate outputs throughout this process, checking report support,
timepoint alignment, visual evidence availability, answer format validity,
redaction, and scoring consistency. Appendix

blocks.en: 3.4 Quality Control
blocks.zh: 3.4 质量控制

blocks.en:
BrainTRACE stores a non-model-facing hidden reference for each item, including the target answer, required supporting facts, clinically material contradictions, and scoring criteria. Closed-form items use a lightly normalized target answer. Open-ended items use a rubric of required facts, optional facts, and record contradicting statements. For case reasoning items, each decomposed VQA step has its own reference, so the evaluation can identify where the evidence path breaks. The case reasoning track receives item level review by an American Board of
Radiology (ABR) certified radiation oncologist, including the question,
ground truth, and audit rubric for each decomposed step.

BrainTRACE为每个项目存储了一个非模型化的隐性参考,包括目标答案,需要证明的事实,临床上的材料自相矛盾,以及评分标准. 封闭式物品使用轻度常态化的目标解答. 不限成员名额的项目使用所要求的事实、可选事实和相互矛盾的陈述的记录。 对于案例推理项目,每个被分解的VQA步骤都有自己的参考,因此评价可以确定证据路径的断点. 案件推理轨道得到美国人权委员会的项目级别审查。

blocks.en:
BrainTRACE controls leakage by separating inputs from hidden clinical records. During evaluation, models receive only the rendered visual evidence, the question, the answer format, and allowed non-leaking metadata. They do not receive radiology reports, parsed report fields, segmentation masks, measurement tables, or hidden reference fields.
Metadata is redacted when it could reveal the answer. Each instance
passes quality control checks for redaction, report support, visual
evidence availability, and scoring consistency. We also run text-only
leakage probes to test whether the question wording alone is sufficient
to infer the answer without visual evidence.

blocks.en: 4.1 Experimental Setup

blocks.en:
We evaluate 20 model configurations spanning open-weight general VLMs,
open-weight medical VLMs, closed-source frontier VLMs, and available
native-volume medical baselines (Table 2 ). All
models are evaluated zero-shot using only the permitted model-facing
visual evidence, question, answer format, and allowed non-leaking
metadata. Reports, segmentation masks, parsed findings, measurements, and
hidden reference fields are never shown. Each model receives one attempt
per item. Malformed outputs, refusals, and abstentions remain in the
denominator. For 3D evidence items, general VLMs use released rendered
inputs, while native-volume medical baselines use their supported
volume input interfaces. Thus, 3D evidence results compare supported
interfaces on shared clinical targets rather than isolating native-volume
representation as a controlled variable.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
We introduced BrainTRACE , a report-grounded benchmark for
longitudinal brain MRI VLM evaluation. BrainTRACE asks whether models can
trace evidence across serial studies, MRI sequences, volumetric anatomy,
and report-derived clinical references, rather than answer isolated image
questions. The main finding is not simply that current VLMs score low, but
that their successes do not compose: local recognition rarely survives
through longitudinal, report-grounded clinical synthesis. This gap persists
under current 3D evidence and native-volume interfaces, suggesting that
volumetric access alone is insufficient without stronger multi-sequence,
temporal, and evidence-grounded reasoning. We release the benchmark
specification, evaluation lists, scoring implementation, factual audit protocol, and audit record format to support reproducible evaluation of
future brain MRI VLMs. Limitations and responsible-use considerations are summarized in Appendix G .

blocks.en: B.2 Upstream MR-RATE source and retained follow-up cohort

blocks.en:
BrainTRACE is constructed from MR-RATE [ 12 ] , a public
MRI corpus with paired clinical radiology reports. The upstream corpus
contains 83,425 patients, 98,334 MRI studies, and 705,254 MRI
series or metadata rows. BrainTRACE retains the longitudinal subset
needed for follow-up reasoning: 1,778 patients, 7,299 MRI studies,
and 65,974 series-level metadata rows, with at least three MRI
studies per retained patient. This source design makes provenance
auditable and keeps the references grounded in authentic, anonymized
radiology reports rather than generated report text. It does not imply
population representativeness for all neuroradiology indications.
BrainTRACE does not redistribute raw imaging or model-facing reports;
users obtain upstream MR-RATE access under its terms, and evaluated
models receive only the visual evidence permitted by each task.

BrainTRACE organizes questions by the clinical reasoning depth required to
answer them, rather than treating all items as interchangeable visual
recognition tasks. The levels therefore define what kind of evidence
operation is being tested; they are not merely ordered difficulty bins.

blocks.en: C.1 Factual-audit scoring for open-ended and case-level answers

blocks.en:
Open-ended and case-level answers are scored by factual clinical audit
rather than lexical similarity. A response passes only if it covers the
required clinical facts, satisfies the critical rubric slots, avoids
clinically material contradictions, and does not introduce unsupported
claims that would alter the interpretation. This distinction is
necessary for radiology-style answers: fluent prose can still fail if it
changes laterality, reverses interval direction, assigns a finding to
the wrong anatomy, cites the wrong timepoint, or asserts an unsupported
disease-status conclusion.

evidence quotations, or construction record. All evaluated outputs use
the same judge model version, instruction text, response schema, and
deterministic decoding setting, and the complete judge record is
archived for each item.

blocks.en:
For each item or decomposed case step, the judge record contains the
following fields. These fields define the scoring variables used in the
reported metrics: • required_fact_results : checks whether named findings,
locations, laterality, timepoints, trajectory direction, and current
status required by the reference are explicitly present or clinically
equivalent. • slot_results : evaluates each rubric slot against the
model answer. Critical slots enter the pass rule; noncritical slots
are retained for coverage and quality analyses. • critical_errors : records hard contradictions such as
wrong anatomy, wrong laterality, wrong interval direction, wrong
timepoint, wrong modality-specific reading, wrong diagnosis, or
clinically material severity errors. • unsupported_claims : records claims not supported by the
reference or rubric, such as a new lesion, disease progression,
treatment response, or diagnosis absent from the clinical reference. • clinically_acceptable : gives the final rubric-based
factual verdict used for Pass %. • quality_score : records graded answer quality on the
same 1–5 clinical scale used in the human validation subset.

The calibration prevents levels with higher answer-option floors from
appearing easier than they are. For example, GPT-5 has higher raw L3

interpretation: recognition-level strength does not imply reliable

The latest-timepoint condition retains the current study but removes
prior longitudinal studies. Its paired accuracy drop measures dependence
on serial context, including interval change and trajectory evidence.
The T2-only condition retains the longitudinal T2 series but removes

contrast and sequence-specific findings, including enhancement or
susceptibility cues when those are needed by the reference. The no-image
condition withholds visual inputs while keeping the same question and
answer space. Its drop measures residual dependence on question text,
answer priors, or permitted non-image cues when rendered MRI evidence is
absent.

blocks.en: Appendix G Limitations and Responsible Use
blocks.zh: 附录G 限制和负责任的使用

blocks.en:
BrainTRACE evaluates longitudinal reasoning over brain MRI follow-up
studies in an MR-RATE-derived cohort. Its task families assume
multi-sequence brain imaging, English language radiology reports, and
cases with sufficient follow-up, report, and segmentation-derived
evidence. It is not intended to represent other anatomies,
other languages, one-off clinical referrals with sparse longitudinal
context, or the full spectrum of neuroradiology indications. Its scores
are designed for reproducible
model comparison, not for estimating absolute clinical performance.
Users should report per-level, per-attribute, and acquisition subgroup
results rather than treating a single aggregate score as a clinical
capability measure.

blocks.en:
The benchmark is report-grounded rather than independently re-read from
scratch. The references come from authentic MR-RATE clinical radiology
reports and segmentation-derived measurements, and released questions,
ground truth, and audit fields pass construction and consistency checks.
The case reasoning track further receives item-level review by an
ABR-certified radiation oncologist. Even with these controls, reports
are clinical documents rather than pixel-level annotations. A report may
compress timepoints, omit a visually apparent but clinically secondary
finding, or express uncertainty, and segmentation-derived measurements
can carry registration, acquisition, and algorithmic error. Scores
should be read as agreement with the reviewed, report-grounded
clinical references under the released benchmark specification, not as a
new adjudicated imaging diagnosis or deployment certification. The
primary open-ended scores use a GPT family factual audit judge, and a
small cross-family audit in Appendix C.6 shows judge family sensitivity for GPT-5.4 outputs. The
3D evidence track tests a clinically important evidence condition, but
its rendered 16-slice and native-volume pathways introduce an
input interface confound. These results should be read as
comparisons among available model interfaces on shared clinical targets,
not as a controlled ablation of 3D representation alone. BrainTRACE
releases evaluation records for audit, but it does not redistribute raw
imaging. Users must obtain access to the upstream MR-RATE
corpus [ 12 ] and follow the corresponding data-use terms.
